_about: How an online source is doing, as the person sees it on home, the Source page and the setup's Connect step (docs/44
'Living with two apps', Appendix C 'States and exits'): one state from the last call's outcome, whether the device
has a network, and the newest reading's age. 'outcome': null = nothing asked yet; 'ok' = the site answered; 'network'
= no answer (DNS, TLS, timeout, refused connection); 'server' = 5xx or an answer that isn't the site's; 'notFound' =
404 (not a Nightscout at that address); 'refused' = 401 / 403 (the token or API secret); 'rateLimited' = 429.
States: 'connecting' (the first call is on its way), 'live' (the newest reading is at most 'late_after_s' old),
'late' (older, up to 'silent_after_s': readings come in gaps), 'noNewReadings' (older still, or the site has none:
it answers but nothing new reaches it; the uploader is the place to look), 'offline' (no network on this device:
it catches up when it's back), 'unreachable' (a network but no answer from the site: down, or the address is wrong),
'signedOut' (refused: enter the token again; nothing is asked again until then or 'refused_s'), 'rateLimited'
(the site asked to wait). A refusal or a rate limit says so whatever the network; a failure is 'offline' only
when the device has no network. The no-data alert still counts from the reading's time (contracts/alerts/SPEC.md).
LibreLinkUp adds three outcomes (docs/44 step 2): 'terms' = the login asks to accept new terms or a new privacy
policy (status 4): 'actionNeeded', the person opens LibreLinkUp and accepts them (Sukrara never accepts for them);
'notShared' = the account follows no one, or no longer the person picked: 'notShared'; 'retired' = Abbott's API
refuses this client (a version Sukrara can't send, an endpoint gone): 'stopped', said plainly (an update of Sukrara
may bring it back). These three say so whatever the network, as a refusal does.
'warmingUp' (default false) = the source's sensor, by its sensor life (the start the source gives, the warm-up
contracts/sensor/life.json sets, SensorTiming.warming: no reading since its start), is in its warm-up: an answer
('ok') then says 'warmingUp' (the sensor warming up, ready at its warm-up's end) whatever the newest reading's age,
since the newest reading is the old sensor's and nothing new can come before then (owner's test, 2026-11-18: a new
Libre 3 read as 'nothing new … it may have stopped uploading'). A problem, no network or nothing asked yet still
says so.
